title: Just-in-Time Delegated Admin Workflow and Priority Triage
creator: Marco Reyes
description: Customers (mid-market and enterprise) repeatedly request short-lived elevated admin access to complete onboarding, entitlement changes, or emergency troubleshooting. Current intake is manual (email + form) and high-friction for both customers and Redwood support, creating long wait times and inconsistent audit trails. This ticket defines a just-in-time (JIT) delegated admin workflow plus a triage rubric to prioritize non-bug admin/access requests (RBAC templates, SSO/SAML mapping, SCIM provisioning changes, org policy exceptions). The goal is a reproducible intake flow that reduces mean time to grant (MTTG), preserves auditability, and minimizes security exposure.
acceptance_criteria: A documented JIT delegated admin intake flow exists in Confluence with step-by-step paths for: temporary role grants, manager approval, auto-expiry, and audit logs
An automated triage rubric (low/medium/high risk) that uses requester role, scope, and customer SLA to assign priority and target SLA is defined and stored as JSON in the intake service
Integration design with SSO/SAML claim mapping and SCIM provisioning endpoints is reviewed with Eng and Security and has a clear compatibility matrix for top 5 enterprise IdPs
A minimal POC flow in staging that demonstrates: request submission, approver notification, issuance of temporary admin role via SCIM or internal API, and automatic revocation after TTL
Runbook for support & security including escalation path, logs to retention pipeline, and audit query examples

notes: 2026-02-22 meeting: Customers want 1-8 hour admin windows; security prefers max 24 hours and strong approver verification
Decision: prefer delegated roles over direct account elevation to keep SCIM mapping consistent with customer IdP
Tradeoff: fully-automated approvals are faster but risk-prone for high-scope requests; we will allow auto-approval for scoped, low-risk requests only
We will store triage rules in the intake service feature-flagged for a gradual rollout
Observed: several enterprise customers also asked for a 'just-in-time SCIM sync' option for group membership changes — potential follow-up

risk_assessment: Risk: unauthorized privilege escalation if approver identity is spoofed. Mitigation: require SSO/IdP verification or cross-check against org manager claim.
Risk: audit log gaps during auto-provisioning. Mitigation: instrument synchronous write to audit pipeline before issuing temporary role
Risk: SCIM compatibility varies by vendor. Mitigation: define compatibility matrix and fallback to internal token issuance for unsupported IdPs
Operational risk: manual support revocation may be needed for edge cases. Mitigation: training and runbook for on-call and support
follow_up: Run a 2-week pilot with 2 enterprise customers and collect MTTG metrics
Iterate on triage rules based on pilot data and security feedback
Add UI telemetry to measure drop-off in request form and friction points
Expand supported IdPs in compatibility matrix after pilot
